title: POC scoping: success criteria signoff - Nimbus Health
next_steps: Redwood to share formal success-criteria doc and acceptance-tests spreadsheet by 2025-11-14
Schedule initial benchmark run (hosted) w/ sample data on 2025-11-20
Customer to provide 5k representative queries + sample dataset by 2025-11-18
Nimbus to spin up test VPC/peering and provide test creds by 2025-11-17
Redwood SE to deliver baseline performance report within 48h of benchmark completion
action_items: Lena Patel: Send formal POC contract and pricing options (due 2025-11-14)
Marco Li: Prepare benchmark harness, baseline script, and instrumentation (due 2025-11-18)
Priya Shah: Provide 5k representative queries, example documents, and success labels (due 2025-11-18)
Daniel Brooks: Setup VPC peering/test account and share firewall rules (due 2025-11-17)
Omar Velasquez: Confirm SOC 2 artifacts and provide compliance contact (due 2025-11-16)
summary: POC scoping call to finalize success criteria and acceptance tests for Nimbus Health. Agreed on explicit go/no-go thresholds (latency, error rates, accuracy), dataset and workload sizing (5k queries, avg 150 tokens), benchmark cadence and reporting format (CSV + dashboard + raw logs). Action items assigned and timeline for initial hosted benchmark set for 2025-11-20.
transcript:
00:00 Lena Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check - audio okay?
00:04 Priya Shah: Yep, loud and clear.
00:06 Marco Li: Great. We'll run through the success criteria doc and acceptance tests then lock dates.
00:11 Kathy Miller: We've had a couple internal talks about latency and data residency, so want to make sure those are explicit.
00:18 Lena Patel: Totally. Marco, do you want to start with the performance thresholds?
00:22 Marco Li: Sure. For the POC we proposed p50 latency under 200 ms, p95 under 500 ms for our text-generation path with avg payload ~150 tokens. Sustained throughput target is 50 qps for the core inference route, bursts to 120 qps acceptable for 30s. Error rate target below 1%, tolerable up to 2% as a warning - anything above 2% is a fail.
00:48 Priya Shah: For our workloads the distribution is spiky during peak hours - is the 50 qps the steady-state or peak?
00:53 Marco Li: 50 qps is steady-state for the test; we'll run a separate burst test to validate autoscaling and the dedicated pool behaviour.
00:58 Daniel Brooks: Quick question - how are you measuring tokens? edge tokens or model tokens? We need consistent accounting for cost comparisons.
01:04 Marco Li: We'll use model-side tokenization (the tokenizer the model uses) as our baseline. We will include raw counts in the report so you can map to your cost models.
01:11 Priya Shah: For accuracy, we care about both ranking precision and hallucination rate. Can we define acceptance metrics?
01:16 Lena Patel: Yes. Suggested accuracy thresholds: intent classification or routing accuracy >= 92% on labeled set, top-1 relevancy precision >= 88% for retrieval-augmented responses, and hallucination incidence under 0.5% on the test set. If hallucination > 1% that's a hard fail for the POC.
01:33 Kathy Miller: That hallucination threshold seems tight but okay for PII-sensitive clinical content.
01:38 Omar Velasquez: On the security side, we need to ensure no unredacted PHI leaves our VPC during dedicated runs. For hosted runs we need RBAC and audit logs for all query payloads and responses.
01:49 Marco Li: We can provide audit log exports and you can run the redaction tests. For dedicated/private we support customer-managed KMS; we'll provide instructions in the security doc.
01:57 Daniel Brooks: Are you planning to do both hosted and dedicated benchmarks? We want to see the delta.
02:01 Marco Li: Yes. Phase 1: hosted run with representative dataset (this week), Phase 2: dedicated run (if accepted) - typically a 1- or 2-GPU pool for the initial throughput target; we'll size after baseline. We'll include a quantized variant test (8-bit) for cost/latency tradeoffs.
02:17 Priya Shah: Workload sizing - we mentioned 5k queries. Are those per day? total test set?
02:21 Marco Li: For the POC acceptance tests we want a static test corpus of 5,000 representative queries to run deterministically against the model endpoints. We'll also run a concurrency test with synthetic load to validate autoscaling: 20 concurrent clients for steady state, and a 120 qps burst test.
02:34 Lena Patel: Reporting format - we'll deliver the benchmark report as: CSV of raw responses and latencies, a summary dashboard link, a JSON of aggregated metrics, and raw logs. Do you want an additional scoring sheet?
02:42 Priya Shah: CSV + dashboard is good. Also we'd like a simple scoring sheet that maps each acceptance criterion to pass/fail and notes.
02:48 Marco Li: We'll produce an acceptance-tests spreadsheet that lists criteria, measurement method, dataset used, p50/p95/p99, error rates, accuracy metrics, and a final go/no-go column.
02:57 Kathy Miller: What are the explicit go/no-go thresholds again? Let's call them out so we can sign off.
03:01 Marco Li: Call out list: p50 < 200 ms (goal), p95 < 500 ms (threshold), if p95 > 700 ms -> fail. Error rate > 2% -> fail. Hallucination > 1% -> fail. Intent accuracy < 90% -> fail (we recommend >=92%). Throughput: if sustained 50 qps can't be maintained for 10 minutes under test then fail. Data exfiltration or failure to produce audit logs -> immediate fail.
03:26 Priya Shah: OK that seems clear. For acceptance tests we'll also need the test harness to be reproducible - can you commit to running the harness inside our VPC for the dedicated run?
03:33 Marco Li: Yes we can run the harness from a customer procured test VM in your VPC, or we can provide a containerized harness you run. Either works; for compliance we prefer the customer-run harness so logs never leave your network until you opt in.
03:46 Lena Patel: We'll note that in the POC doc. What about quality monitoring and regression checks? We want to make sure model behavior is stable across runs.
03:53 Marco Li: We'll run three repeat runs and compute confidence intervals for p50/p95 and model metrics. We'll also run a small regression check against your golden set of 200 critical prompts. If regression > 5% on that set we flag it.
04:06 Daniel Brooks: Network considerations - we'll need instructions for VPC peering and required ports. Also what about TLS and mutual auth?
04:12 Marco Li: We'll share an ops checklist with ports and a sample terraform snippet for peering. We support mTLS for dedicated/private and standard TLS for hosted. KMS integration will be documented.
04:21 Kathy Miller: Ok timeline recap?
04:23 Lena Patel: Action items: Redwood shares success-criteria doc by Friday 2025-11-14, Nimbus to provide dataset by Monday 2025-11-18, setup peering by 2025-11-17, initial hosted benchmark 2025-11-20.
04:33 Priya Shah: Can you also include a sample of the CSV columns you'll provide?
04:36 Marco Li: Yes: request_id, timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, tokenizer_bytes, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, status_code, error_message, top1_label, hallucination_flag, full_response, model_version, run_id.
04:51 Omar Velasquez: On compliance, we'll need to review SOC2 docs and a data processing addendum before any data leaves our environment.
04:56 Lena Patel: We'll attach SOC2 report and DPAs as part of the security packet.
05:00 Kathy Miller: Anything else? Cost questions came up - can you provide an estimated cost delta for hosted vs dedicated per 1M tokens?
05:06 Marco Li: We can provide a modeled estimate post-baseline; ballpark: hosted higher due to multi-tenant overhead, dedicated lowers per-token but has reserved cost. We'll include a cost table in the POC deliverable.
05:16 Priya Shah: Ok I'm comfortable to sign off on these criteria pending the formal doc. We'll need to have leadership review but this is the set we can agree to in principle.
05:23 Lena Patel: Great - we'll send the doc and acceptance spreadsheet. Any last Qs?
05:28 Daniel Brooks: None from infra.
05:30 Omar Velasquez: None.
05:32 Lena Patel: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the files and schedule the hosted run for 11/20.
05:36 End of recording

Notes: Transcript contains some auto-captions mistakes and occasional speaker overlap; names sometimes abbreviated. Shared artifacts: link to "POC success criteria deck" (drive.redwood/example) and "acceptance-tests spreadsheet" (drive.redwood/acceptance/nimbus).
